reason: Excluded on 2026-10-01: the published estimates are incomplete (Q, IIV and residual error not openly reported; linear clearance differs tenfold between reports of the same group) and the public dataset holds 321 of the 443 concentrations, so no verifiable reference model exists; a PKPy2 fit of the reported structure did not converge in 30 minutes.

entry.source: nlmixr2data::nimoData (R package nlmixr2data 2.0.10), DV converted from log to natural scale by prepare_data.py; Rodriguez-Vera et al. 2015
entry.description: Nimotuzumab, a humanized anti-EGFR IgG1 monoclonal antibody, in 12 women with advanced breast cancer. Three patients each received 50, 100, 200 or 400 mg as intravenous infusions (0.4 to 3 hours) once weekly for about 10 weeks, with serum sampling over 94 days (24 to 28 samples per patient). Columns: ID; TIME in hours; AMT dose in mg and RATE infusion rate in mg/h (dose records); DV serum nimotuzumab concentration in ug/mL (mg/L); OCC dosing occasion; EVID and MDV follow NONMEM conventions; WGT weight in kg (recorded per occasion); BSA body surface area in m2; AGE in years; HGT height in cm; DOS dose level in mg.
entry.knowledge: Nimotuzumab shows target-mediated drug disposition through binding to EGFR: describe it with a two-compartment quasi-steady-state TMDD model with interindividual variability on clearance, central volume and KSS, and no covariate effects.

reference.source: Rodriguez-Vera L et al. J Clin Pharmacol 2015;55:888-898 (model structure, abstract); estimates from the same group's WCP2018 abstract (doi:10.1254/jpssuppl.WCP2018.0_PO1-8-42)
reference.model: two-compartment QSS-TMDD with target synthesis (ksyn), degradation (kdeg) and complex internalization (kint); lognormal IIV on CL, V1 and KSS; additive error on log concentrations; no covariates
reference.note: Q, the IIV variances and the residual SD are not openly reported. A 2020 paper of the same group cites CL = 0.00703 L/h, ten times the WCP2018 value. The public dataset has 321 of the 443 concentrations of the original analysis.
